tasks.title: Component-literal scanner as a Rust test whose needles come from the LIVE registry, with a counted allowlist
tasks.gate: §19.3 production literal scanner planted-positive; three mandatory reverse cases (a) discovery-derived needle (b) namespaced FQN (c) un-allowlisted new module

plantedFailure.edit: plant the namespaced FQN `lingxi-local-app:local-app-build` (NOT the basename) into harness-runtime/src/mobile/local_apps_host.rs

tasks.notes:
§19.3's literal wording — `tasks/src` and `tools/workflow/src` contain no Local App workflow basename — CANNOT be green on landing, because Phase -1 step 1 explicitly KEEPS both existing registrations (tools/workflow/src/builtins.rs plus three .js files in that directory). Ship the allowlist explicit and counted, reaching 0 only at Phase 9. Without the count, the obvious way to make the red gate green is to exempt the directory, which silently disables the scanner for all of tools/workflow/. The count is the thing that makes that visible.

SCOPED AT lap/baseline. §19.3's reverse case (a) as written needs a verified Plugin inventory, which does not exist until Phase 0a/2. §18 step 7 is explicit that Phase -1 derives needles from the EXISTING live registries and Phase 2 switches to Plugin inventory. At Phase -1 the live source is mobile_skill_registry() (harness-runtime/src/mobile/mod.rs:383 -> skill_api::register_mobile), so case (a) becomes: add a skill to the live registry, confirm the needle set GROWS, then plant that new name in local_apps_host.rs and require red. That is why this is a Rust test and not a python grep gate — a python scanner cannot call into the registry, and a needle list it kept itself would be the static array the gate exists to forbid.

KNOWN COUPLING, adjudicated after the write stage. The scanner's WORKFLOW needles are derived from `tool_workflow::LOCAL_APP_BUILD_WORKFLOWS` (tools/workflow/src/lib.rs:310) — which is the array P-1.9 DELETES. This is an ordering defect in the decomposition, not in the writer's judgment: P-1.0 was sequenced first and pointed at P-1.9's deletion target. The alternative live source, `BUILTIN_WORKFLOWS` (tools/workflow/src/builtins.rs:93), does survive Phase -1 — Phase -1 step 1 keeps both registrations — but it also contains `deep-research`, and no property distinguishing a Local App workflow from it exists until P-1.6 introduces LocalAppWorkflowTaskScope. So the bootstrap is real. Resolution: keep this source, and make P-1.9 responsible for re-pointing the scanner. When P-1.9 deletes the array this test FAILS TO COMPILE, which is loud and correct. The only wrong resolution is hardcoding the two names here — that turns the gate into the static array it exists to forbid.

tasks.title: Workspace lease reads the typed scope; delete the tasks/src workflow-name list
tasks.gate: §19.3 a custom workflow with the same name gets NO workspace lease

plantedFailure.edit: reinstate the LOCAL_APP_BUILD_WORKFLOWS array at tasks/src/lib.rs:37 and key the lease off it

tasks.notes:
MEASURED BLAST RADIUS (re-grounded before P-1.6 started). `tasks::LOCAL_APP_BUILD_WORKFLOWS` has 5 reader sites, of which the two that matter are `tasks/src/registry.rs:918` and `tasks/src/handlers/local_workflow.rs:523` — both PRODUCTION and both outside `tasks/src/lib.rs`, which is all this descriptor's `owns` currently names. Add both files to the owned set when this task runs, or it cannot delete the array it is asked to delete.

🚨 FOUR GREEN-BY-CONSTRUCTION HAZARDS, handed over by P-1.6's verify pass. Each was demonstrated or traced, not speculated.

(a) THE Option<scope> FALLBACK. The natural incremental migration is `scope: Option<..>` with `match scope { Some(s) => s.requires_workspace_lease(), None => LOCAL_APP_BUILD_WORKFLOWS.contains(..) }`. Every new test builds a Some, so the None arm is never exercised and stays green FOREVER — while every launch this task misses, and every task row persisted before the migration, takes the name-derived arm. P-1.9 would then 'delete the array' by inlining the two literals into that arm.

(b) SCAN-ROOT BLIND SPOT. coordinator/, cron/ and apps/cli/ all depend on `tasks` and NONE is a component-scanner root (SCAN_ROOTS = engine-mobile/src, tasks/src, tools/workflow/src). A fallback that lands in any of them is invisible to that gate.

(c) THE DELETE GUARD CAN ONLY WEAKEN. blocks_delete() is a constant true, so the type cannot express 'this row carries no authority' — that discrimination necessarily lives in the Option. If find_nonterminal_local_app_workflows (registry.rs:918) is rewritten as 'rows whose scope is Some', any Local App workflow launched without a scope stops blocking delete entirely and the App becomes deletable mid-build. Required tests, renamed by P-1.8 because the original name I wrote was ambiguous — "no scope" reads as `scope: None`, which per §8.1 must grant NOTHING, while the test actually pins a `Some` with a non-Build purpose: a_build_purpose_blocks_delete_at_the_guard (control), a_use_test_purpose_still_blocks_delete_at_the_guard, an_mcp_authoring_purpose_still_blocks_delete_at_the_guard.

(d) THE PREDICATES ARE ADVISORY. Nothing forces a caller to consult requires_workspace_lease(). Keeping the old name check ALONGSIDE the typed one as 'defense in depth' restores the exact grant while the suite stays green, because the typed path also works. This task's stated gate covers only the MODEL DEFAULT — not the lease, not the delete guard. Required test: a_custom_workflow_with_the_same_name_gets_no_lease_and_does_not_block_delete.

INHERITED FOLLOW-UP from P-1.6. scope.rs mirrors local_apps::ids::is_valid_app_id's grammar with a corpus copied from that crate's own tests, because adding a production `local-apps` edge to `tasks` would drag bundled SQLite, vendored libgit2 and two tree-sitter grammars into a crate with 5 dependents for a 6-line predicate. A DEV-dependency is the right answer — check_deps.py excludes dev deps, so it is gate-legal and costs production builds nothing — and it enables a real cross-crate agreement test. Until then the two corpora can drift silently. tasks/Cargo.toml is now owned for this.

⚠️ AND THE LIMIT P-1.6 COULD NOT CLOSE: the type guarantees the PURPOSE is the Host's choice and the app_id is well formed. It does NOT guarantee OWNERSHIP — `for_build("victim-app")` succeeds, because the type cannot know entitlement. §8.1 requires defending a forged `args.app_id`; that half is THIS task's obligation. The Host MUST take app_id from the resolved LocalAppPluginBinding handle, never from caller args. scope.rs's `a_well_formed_victim_app_id_is_still_accepted` encodes the limit so it cannot be mistaken for a guarantee.

tasks.title: Cut the workflow-name trigger binding in skill-api, and pin the two look-alikes that must NOT be touched
tasks.gate: §19.3 no Local App component name carries authority outside the composition binding

plantedFailure.edit: restore "local-app-build" to the create-local-app skill's triggers array in bundled.rs

tasks.notes:
FOUND BY THE P-1.0 VERIFICATION PASS, outside the three scan roots, and confirmed by hand at lap/baseline.

THE DEFECT. skill-api/src/builtin/bundled.rs:43 gives the create-local-app SKILL the trigger array ["create local app", "local app", "local-app-build"]. The third entry is a WORKFLOW name used as a skill trigger phrase — a cross-component name binding, which is exactly the shape §19.3 exists to remove. It is genuine production code: there is no #[cfg(test)] above that line. Phase 4 merges the two workflows, at which point this trigger silently stops matching and nothing in the suite notices. The skill NAMES in the same file are the definition site and are legitimately unscannable; the trigger is not.

⛔ THE LOOK-ALIKE THAT MUST NOT BE 'FIXED'. platform-api/src/mobile_linux.rs:46 declares LOCAL_APP_BUILD_ROOT = "/var/lingxi/local-app-build". That string coincides with a workflow name but is a FILESYSTEM MOUNT ROOT, not a reference to the workflow. It carries no name-derived authority, and renaming it to track a renamed workflow would silently move a path on real devices — the same class of silent data loss as renaming a SQLite table, which nothing in this repo would catch. Add it to the allowlist with this reasoning if traits/src ever enters the scan surface; do not touch the value.

TEMPLATES, for the record. local-apps/templates/runtime-profiles/** is compiled into production wholesale by include_bytes! via the profile_file! macro, and the scanner cannot see it. Grepped at lap/baseline: it contains ZERO component-name needles today. That is a fact with a date on it, not a guarantee — it is the tree runtime-profile work touches, so the Phase 1 packer (P1.2) should carry the assertion rather than this scanner.

SCOPE. Deliberately NOT solved by widening SCAN_ROOTS. Adding skill-api/src and traits/src would make the scanner red on landing for two occurrences of very different kinds, and the cheapest way to green that is an allowlist entry — which would preserve the defect while looking like it had been handled.

RE-GROUNDED before the task starts. The must-name `bundled.rs` has zero hits as file CONTENT — expected, since it is a path, not a symbol. It can therefore only reach the output if the test PRINTS the path in its failure message. That is a real constraint on how the test must be written, not a free property: an assertion that fails with `assert!(!triggers.contains(...))` and no message would satisfy the gate's `failures:` requirement while never naming the file, and the gate would pass. Write the assertion with a message naming skill-api/src/builtin/bundled.rs.
Verified still present at re-grounding time: bundled.rs contains the `local-app-build` trigger.

tasks.title: Re-mint the Local App workflow scope at the restart-adoption seam
tasks.gate: §19.3 a build in flight across an engine restart still blocks its App's delete

plantedFailure.edit: drop the re-minted scope at register_adopted_workflow so an adopted row carries scope: None

tasks.notes:
DISCLOSED RESIDUAL from P-1.7's fix round, narrower than what it replaced but real. register_adopted_workflow (tasks/src/registry.rs:1078) sets scope: None, so a Local App build that was in flight across an engine restart comes back Paused — non-terminal — and does NOT block its app's delete. The pre-P-1.7 name-based guard DID block it.

Window: engine restart during a build, then the user deletes that app. Narrow, but a real loss of a protection that existed before.

⛔ IT CANNOT BE CLOSED BY READING THE CHECKPOINT. The checkpoint records whatever the original caller supplied, so a custom workflow's checkpoint carries its forged args.app_id just as faithfully as a real build's — trusting it reopens exactly the vector P-1.7 closed. Closing it means RE-MINTING at the adoption seam from state the Host re-resolves on load: the app still exists, is still scaffolded, and is still pinned to the adopted workflow_id. AdoptedWorkflow has no way to express that today.

The framing to keep, corrected during P-1.7 (P-1.6's doc and my brief both had it wrong): the app_id must be one the Host RESOLVED, not one it was TOLD. The LocalAppPluginBinding handle names a WORKFLOW, not an app, so 'take the app_id from the binding handle' was impossible as written.

🚨 A SECOND TRIPWIRE THIS TASK MUST CARRY, from P-1.7's verify pass. `TaskState` still derives `Deserialize`, and `#[serde(skip)]` on the scope field means it defaults to `None` on any future read-back — with NO compile error. So the day a persistence seam lands, the delete guard silently reverts to exactly today's adoption gap, and nothing fails. state.rs's doc says to re-mint at that seam; a doc is not a mechanism. Land a compile-time or test-time tripwire together with the seam.

Also recorded from that pass: only `for_build` is ever minted in production — `for_use_test` and `for_mcp_authoring` have no call sites outside tests. `blocks_delete()`'s 'every purpose blocks' contract is therefore UNEXERCISED in production. Not a regression (the old name-based guard covered strictly less), but the three-purpose surface is aspirational until the use-test and MCP-authoring workflows get their own mint.
